messages:
sara (docs): Quick doc bug: API ref for /v1/generate lists temperature range as 0.00.0 with default 1.0, but our examples and SDK snippets use 1.2 in a toy demo. Users are confused.

leo (ml): The runtime supports >1.0. Temperature is unbounded in implementation; values >1 amplify randomness. We historically documented 01 to try to discourage extreme numbers, but that's inconsistent.

matt (sdk): SDK validation currently clamps to <=2.0 to catch obvious typos, but we log a warning. That clamping is why some tests fail when docs use 5.0 in an example.

sara (docs): Proposal: update API ref to show temperature: float (>=0) with "typical range 0.00.0; values >1 increase randomness" and change examples to use 0.7/1.0 instead of 1.2 or 5.0. Also add an SDK note about client-side clamping.

leo (ml): Agree. Also add a note about deterministic models: for some models temperature is ignored when sampling is disabled. We should point to model behavior in the model catalog.

matt (sdk): I'll update SDK snippets and relax clamp behavior to accept >2.0 while keeping a lint warning. I'll open a docs+sdk PR together to keep examples and validation in sync.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/821 by matt (sdk)  checks triggered

sara (docs): Checklist: 1) update API ref field description 2) change code examples to show 0.7/1.0 3) add note linking to model catalog for model-specific behavior 4) add SDK validation note.

matt (sdk): PR includes updated examples in docs/reference/generate.md and minor SDK docs. Running linkcheck.

ci-bot: All checks passed for PR #821.

matt (sdk): Merged. I'll add a short SDK changelog entry about relaxed clamp and lint warning.

sara (docs): Draft release blurb: "Docs: clarified temperature parameter semantics and example values. Use 0.7 for creative sampling; values >1 increase randomness. SDK now warns for very large values."

leo (ml): Thanks all. This should reduce confusion in tutorials.

sara (docs): Closing thread. If you see any other numeric-range mismatches (top_p, repetition_penalty), flag me.
